# whataifound.org

> A curated, independently graded registry of scientific and mathematical results
> discovered by or with AI systems. Every entry is graded on how it was verified and
> how much the AI actually did, so a machine-checked proof is never confused with a
> press release. Negative results (already known, disputed, refuted) stay on the
> record rather than being deleted.

Maintained as an independent editorial project. 190 entries on record. Data is CC BY 4.0; cite as whataifound.org.

## When to use this registry

Reach for this when the question is whether a *specific* claim about an AI discovery
holds up, and to what standard. It is built for four jobs:

- **Checking a claim.** Someone says an AI proved, discovered or solved something.
  Look it up here and read the verification grade: a machine-checked Lean proof and a
  press release are both on this list, and they are not the same thing.
- **Filtering by strength of evidence.** Ask for everything in a field at a given
  grade, for example `https://whataifound.org/api/dataset?field=mathematics&verification=formal`.
- **Separating what the AI did from what people did.** Every entry carries an
  autonomy grade, graded on the strictest defensible reading.
- **Citing one result.** Every finding has its own permanent page with sources, a
  novelty check naming the database and query, and BibTeX.

How to call it: `https://whataifound.org/api/dataset` filters by field, verification, autonomy, lab,
tag or date added, and is described in `https://whataifound.org/openapi.json`. For the whole registry
in one request, take `https://whataifound.org/data/entries.json`.

What it is not: a ranking, a benchmark, or a list of everything AI has ever done. It
is a curated record with a stated grading method, and negative results (already known,
disputed, refuted) stay on it rather than being deleted.

## How entries are graded

Verification, strongest to weakest. When unsure, the lower grade wins:

- **Formally verified**: machine-checked proof (e.g. Lean)
- **Independently checked**: checked by third parties who were not the authors
- **Peer reviewed**: published after peer review
- **Author verified**: verified only by the people who produced it
- **Claimed**: announced, not independently verified
- **Disputed**: substantive public challenge to the result
- **Already known**: correct, but the result already existed in the literature
- **Refuted**: shown to be wrong

Autonomy, most to least AI-driven:

- **Autonomous**: the AI did it without human problem-setting or steering
- **AI-led**: the AI produced the core idea; humans framed or checked it
- **Collaborative**: genuine back-and-forth between AI and human
- **AI-assisted**: humans led; the AI helped with parts
- **Search scaffold**: a human-built search harness (FunSearch, AlphaEvolve) with an LLM inside
- **Retrieval**: the AI located an existing result rather than producing a new one

## Core pages

- [Registry](https://whataifound.org/): all entries, searchable and filterable
- [Methodology](https://whataifound.org/methodology): full definitions of both grading scales and the editorial rules
- [Visuals](https://whataifound.org/visuals): the registry as charts
- [Open review queue](https://whataifound.org/review): entries still needing an independent check
- [Contributors](https://whataifound.org/contributors): who builds and checks the registry
- [Other registries](https://whataifound.org/registries): Palomar, MathDB, vibemathed, ProofAtlas, ClinicalTrials.gov and the FDA AI-enabled device list, what each one certifies, and what none of them do
- [Developers](https://whataifound.org/developers): the API, the bulk downloads and the machine-readable formats, in one place
- [Contact](https://whataifound.org/contact): corrections, submissions and who maintains this

## Data

- [entries.json](https://whataifound.org/data/entries.json): the complete registry, one JSON file, CC BY 4.0
- [/api/dataset](https://whataifound.org/api/dataset): the same registry, filterable by field, verification, autonomy, lab, tag or date added, with a fixed field contract
- [openapi.json](https://whataifound.org/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 for the endpoints above, with every grade vocabulary inlined as an enum
- [entry.schema.json](https://whataifound.org/entry.schema.json): JSON Schema for one entry, the same one the build validates against
- [vocab.json](https://whataifound.org/data/vocab.json): both grade scales with definitions and numeric ratings, source kinds and subject fields
- [RSS](https://whataifound.org/feed.xml) · [JSON Feed](https://whataifound.org/feed.json): new and updated entries

## Findings

### Archaeology

All 1 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/archaeology

- [First Herculaneum scroll read end to end without unrolling it](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-06-25-herculaneum-scroll-read): PHerc. 1667 was virtually unwrapped and read in full from X-ray scans using learned ink detection: about 1.4 metres of papyrus across roughly 22 columns of Greek, identified as Philodemus, On Gods, Book 8. (Vesuvius Challenge, Community-developed ink-detection neural networks, 2026-06-25; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-assisted)

### Astronomy

All 1 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/astronomy

- [An eighth planet around Kepler-90 found by a neural network](https://whataifound.org/finding/2017-12-14-kepler-90i): A convolutional network re-examining Kepler light curves recovered transit signals the standard pipeline had ranked below threshold, yielding Kepler-90i and making Kepler-90 the first star besides the Sun known to host eight planets. (Google Brain / University of Texas at Austin, Convolutional neural network (AstroNet), 2017-12-14; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)

### Biology

All 7 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/biology

- [Agent-run genome survey identifies array-associated reverse transcriptases in jumbo phages](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-09-23-array-associated-reverse-transcriptases): Claude agents surveying reverse transcriptase genes across 1.9 billion metagenomic protein clusters flagged a family of jumbo-phage reverse transcriptases paired with an array of repeated non-coding DNA units and a dedicated partner gene, an arrangement the authors say fits no described reverse transcriptase class. (Anthropic, Claude Mythos 5, 2026-09-23; verification: Claimed; autonomy: Collaborative)
- [AI-generated bacteriophage genomes that replicate and kill bacteria](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-09-17-evo-phage-genomes): Genome language models wrote complete ΦX174-like bacteriophage genomes from scratch; of 285 designs that could be built, 16 produced viable infectious phages, several with faster lysis than the natural virus. (Arc Institute / Stanford University, Evo 1 and Evo 2, 2025-09-17; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Candidate treatment for dry age-related macular degeneration](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-robin-macular): The Robin system automated hypothesis generation, experiment design and data analysis, identifying a novel candidate treatment for dry AMD. (FutureHouse, Robin (multi-agent), 2025-05-01; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [AI co-scientist hypotheses on antimicrobial resistance and liver fibrosis](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-02-ai-coscientist-amr): A multi-agent system generated hypotheses that were subsequently validated experimentally in the lab. (Google, AI Co-Scientist (Gemini 2.0 multi-agent), 2025-02-19; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [A working fluorescent protein generated by a language model](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-01-16-esmgfp): ESM3 designed esmGFP, a bright green fluorescent protein sharing only 58% of its sequence with the closest known natural fluorescent protein, a distance the authors estimate at over 500 million years of natural evolution. (EvolutionaryScale, ESM3 (98B), 2025-01-16; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Joint structure prediction for proteins, nucleic acids and ligands (AlphaFold 3)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-05-08-alphafold3): A diffusion-based successor to AlphaFold predicts complexes spanning proteins, DNA, RNA, small molecules and ions in a single model, with large accuracy gains over the specialised docking tools used for each case. (Google DeepMind / Isomorphic Labs, AlphaFold 3, 2024-05-08; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Accurate protein structure prediction across the known proteome (AlphaFold2)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2021-07-15-alphafold2): AlphaFold2 predicted three-dimensional structures for nearly all catalogued proteins from amino-acid sequence at accuracy rivalling experiment, work that earned the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. (Google DeepMind, AlphaFold2, 2021-07-15; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: AI-led)

### Chemistry

All 3 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/chemistry

- [Enzymes with working catalytic machinery designed from scratch](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-02-13-designed-serine-hydrolases): Diffusion-based protein design produced serine hydrolases with catalytic efficiencies up to \(2.2 \times 10^5\ \mathrm{M^{-1}\,s^{-1}}\) on five folds unlike any natural serine hydrolase, with crystal structures matching the design models to under 1 Å. (Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington, RFdiffusion with PLACER ensemble scoring, 2025-02-13; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [A language-model agent that planned and ran chemistry experiments on lab robots](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-12-20-coscientist): Coscientist, driven by GPT-4 with web search, documentation search, code execution and lab automation, designed and executed palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions on real robotic hardware from a one-line goal. (Carnegie Mellon University, GPT-4 (Coscientist agent), 2023-12-20; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [A new structural class of antibiotic candidates against MRSA](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-12-20-antibiotic-structural-class): Graph neural networks trained on 39,312 assayed compounds and applied to 12 million molecules surfaced a chemical class active against MRSA in mice, with the substructures driving each prediction made explicit rather than left opaque. (MIT / Broad Institute / Harvard, Ensembles of graph neural networks with substructure attribution, 2023-12-20; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)

### Climate science

All 1 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/climate

- [Medium-range weather forecasts from a graph neural network beat the operational physics model](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-11-14-graphcast): GraphCast produced more accurate 10-day forecasts than ECMWF's HRES on roughly 90% of the evaluated variable and lead-time combinations, in under a minute on a single TPU against hours on a supercomputer. (Google DeepMind, GraphCast, 2023-11-14; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)

### Computer science

All 27 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/computer-science

- [NIST elliptic-curve seeds traced to a 1990s C random number generator seeded with the clock](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-16-nist-curve-seeds-lrand48): An Anthropic model showed that the published seeds of the NIST prime curves P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521 and five ANSI X9.62 example curves are outputs of the C library's lrand48 generator seeded with Unix timestamps from May 1997 to April 1998, not hashes of a secret phrase, answering the origin question behind a long-standing backdoor debate. (Anthropic, Internal Anthropic research model (Claude), not named in the announcement, 2026-10-16; verification: Claimed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [LLM-designed quantum circuits with fewer gates and qubits than published designs in seven of eight tasks](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-15-llm-quantum-circuit-design): Claude, run in a loop with an automated evaluator, produced reversible circuits that cut both Toffoli and qubit counts below the best published designs in seven of eight quantum-computing primitives and found a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion in the eighth, including an elliptic-curve point addition with 17 times fewer gates at 12% more qubits. (Anthropic, Claude (the announcement names Claude Mythos 5), 2026-10-15; verification: Claimed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Lower bound of 21 multiplications for 3×3 matrix multiplication over every field, with a Lean proof](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-12-matmul-3x3-rank-21): Andrey Ivanov, working with OpenAI models through ChatGPT and Codex, claims that every exact bilinear algorithm for multiplying two \(3 \times 3\) matrices over any field uses at least 21 multiplications, with a Palomar-registered Lean proof, which would raise the bound that holds over every field from Bläser's 19 of 2003. (Independent, OpenAI models through ChatGPT and Codex, versions not recorded in the repository (GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Sol by the author's later account to vibemathed), 2026-10-12; verification: Claimed; autonomy: Collaborative; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-13-000009; also listed at: vibemathed a-lower-bound-of-21-for-3-3-matrix-multiplication-over-every-field)
- [Matrix multiplication exponent below 2.3710449, machine-checked over every commutative ring](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-07-matmul-exponent-2371045): A Lean development produced largely by AI systems under two researchers' direction proves that the matrix multiplication exponent is below 2.3710449 over every commutative ring, improving DeepMind's 2.371177 of August 2026 by sharing extraction across recursion levels of the laser method. (Independent, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5 and Opus 5.5; Meta Muse Spark 1.3 for the final numerical search, 2026-10-07; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-07-000007)
- [Counterexamples to Zak's modified integer round-down conjecture for the skiving stock problem](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-07-skiving-stock-round-down): A self-published paper claims that the additive integrality gap of the skiving stock (bin covering) problem's pattern LP relaxations is unbounded, refuting Zak's 2003 conjecture that it always stays below two, by transferring OpenAI's unrefereed bin-packing construction; it states that the proof was generated by Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-5.6 Sol Pro. (Independent, Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-5.6 Sol Pro, 2026-10-07; verification: Claimed; autonomy: Collaborative; also listed at: vibemathed zak-s-modified-integer-round-down-conjecture)
- [Matrix multiplication exponent bounded by 9/4](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-06-matmul-exponent-nine-fourths): An OpenAI manuscript proves that two \(n \times n\) complex matrices can be multiplied with \(O(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})\) arithmetic operations, lowering the best bound on the matrix multiplication exponent from 2.371177 to 2.25, with a Lean proof that two outside researchers rebuilt and extended to every field within two days. (OpenAI, Unreleased internal OpenAI model, not named in the release, 2026-10-06; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-08-000005, Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000007; also listed at: vibemathed matrix-multiplication-exponent-9-4)
- [Truly subquadratic 3SUM and truly subcubic APSP, refuting two central fine-grained complexity hypotheses](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-05-3sum-apsp-hypotheses): A preprint by Josh Alman and Virginia Vassilevska Williams gives deterministic algorithms that solve 3SUM on polynomially bounded integers in time \(O(n^{1.9992})\) and all-pairs shortest paths with polynomially bounded integer weights in time \(O(n^{2.9995})\), refuting the 3SUM and APSP hypotheses, from an algorithm the paper says an internal Anthropic model found on its own. (Anthropic, Unreleased internal Anthropic research model (Claude), not named in the paper, 2026-10-05; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led; open-problem record: MathDB 388643; also listed at: vibemathed 3sum-hypothesis, vibemathed apsp-hypothesis)
- [Six-task counterexample to the Kernel Conjecture of pinwheel scheduling](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-09-30-pinwheel-kernel-conjecture): A six-task pinwheel scheduling instance with periods \((3, 4, 5, 20, 22, 36)\) can be scheduled, but not once its longest period is cut to 32, which refutes the Kernel Conjecture and the equivalent \(2^k\) Conjecture of Gąsieniec, Smith and Wild. (Independent, GPT-6 Astra (in OpenAI Codex), 2026-09-30; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; also listed at: vibemathed the-pinwheel-kernel-conjecture-a-six-task-counterexample)
- [Exponential lower bound for the bit pigeonhole principle in unrestricted resolution over parities](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-09-15-bit-php-resolution-over-parities): Any refutation of the bit pigeonhole principle in resolution over parities, a proof system whose lines are disjunctions of linear equations mod 2, must be exponentially long even with no restriction on its depth or regularity; the mathematics was produced by AI models and the main theorem is checked in Lean. (Independent, GPT-6 Astra (mathematics, version 1 formalization and drafting); Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5 (revision 1 formalization), 2026-09-15; verification: Claimed; autonomy: AI-led; also listed at: vibemathed superpolynomial-lower-bounds-for-bit-php-in-unrestricted-resolution-over-paritie)
- [A quantum oracle separating QMA(2) from QMA](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-09-02-qma2-oracle-separation): A quantum oracle is constructed relative to which QMA(2) differs from QMA, resolving Watrous's no-disentanglers conjecture, from a proof idea the authors state was generated by a language model. (MIT / Columbia / University of Washington, ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, 2026-09-02; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-assisted; also listed at: vibemathed a-quantum-oracle-separation-between-mathsf-qma-2-and-mathsf-qma)
- [Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term binary polynomial multiplication](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-31-boolean-multiplicative-complexity-mul4): Multiplying two four-term binary polynomials needs exactly nine AND gates even when nonlinear intermediate wires may be reused, with the whole result formalized in Lean 4. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Opus 5, 2026-08-31; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-assisted; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-09-21-000005; also listed at: vibemathed unrestricted-multiplicative-complexity-mul4)
- [Randomized metric distortion improved to 2.3282](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-29-metric-distortion-23282): A randomized voting rule built on a new random-size stable lottery achieves metric distortion 2.3282, past a 2.5 barrier that existing arguments could not cross. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Opus 5.0, 2026-08-29; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led; also listed at: vibemathed improving-randomized-metric-distortion-to-2-3282)
- [Rapid mixing for spin systems on graphs of girth at least five](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-26-spin-systems-girth-five): Glauber dynamics for proper \(q\)-colourings mixes rapidly once \(q\) exceeds the maximum degree by any fixed factor, provided the graph has girth at least five. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, 2026-08-26; verification: Author verified; autonomy: Collaborative; also listed at: vibemathed rapid-mixing-for-spin-systems-on-graphs-of-girth-at-least-five)
- [Optimal linear encoding rate for lossy compression of Bernoulli sources](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-24-ancheta-massey-linear-coding): Ancheta's answer to Massey's question about linear encoders for lossy compression is extended from the fair-coin case to every source bias below one half. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol, 2026-08-24; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led; also listed at: vibemathed entropy-of-bernoulli-measures-conditioned-on-affine-subspaces-and-a-problem-of-a)
- [Marton's inner bound shown not to reach the broadcast channel capacity region](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-20-marton-inner-bound): There are discrete memoryless broadcast channels whose capacity region is strictly larger than Marton's inner bound, settling in the negative a question open since 1979. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5 and Claude Opus 5, 2026-08-20; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-assisted; open-problem record: MathDB 390544; also listed at: vibemathed marton-inner-bound-capacity-region)
- [Counting linear extensions below the 2ⁿ barrier](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-19-linear-extensions-below-2n): A deterministic algorithm counts the linear extensions of an arbitrary \(n\)-element poset in time \(O^*(1.89^n)\), breaking the \(2^n\) barrier for the general problem. (Independent, Claude Opus 5; ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, 2026-08-19; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led; also listed at: vibemathed counting-linear-extensions-below-two-to-the-n)
- [Matrix multiplication exponent lowered to below 2.371177](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-17-matmul-exponent): A reformulated optimization inside the laser method, with AlphaEvolve applied as the final refinement, lowers the best known upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent from 2.371339 to 2.371177. (Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve, 2026-08-17; verification: Author verified; autonomy: Search scaffold; open-problem record: MathDB 388199; also listed at: vibemathed matrix-multiplication-exponent-2371177)
- [A prescribed Hamiltonian cycle that a book-embedding algorithm cannot produce](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-11-prescribed-cycle-recovery): A 16-vertex graph carries a Hamiltonian cycle that the Alam et al. book-embedding algorithm cannot return for any choice of dual spanning tree, answering a question of Bekos, Kaufmann and Pfister in the negative. (Independent, OpenAI Codex, with Claude for adversarial review, 2026-08-11; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-assisted; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-08-21-000002)
- [Kemeny rank aggregation shown NP-hard for three voters](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-07-28-kemeny-three-voters): Computing a Kemeny-optimal aggregate ranking is NP-hard when the input is exactly three complete rankings, closing the minimal open case left by hardness results for even voter counts. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra, Claude Fable 5, 2026-07-28; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; open-problem record: MathDB 315674; also listed at: vibemathed kemeny-three-voters)
- [Counterexample to the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans conjecture](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-07-22-dinitz-garg-goemans): An explicit seven-node network whose cheapest single-route (unsplittable) shipping costs more than its fractional cost even under the allowed capacity slack, disproving a conjecture from the late 1990s. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Pro, 2026-07-22; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; open-problem record: MathDB 316187; also listed at: vibemathed dinitz-garg-goemans-unsplittable-flow)
- [Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-11-gpt5-science-acceleration): A multi-domain study documenting cases where GPT-5 contributed to research progress across mathematics, physics, biology and materials science. (OpenAI, GPT-5, 2025-11-20; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Limits to black-box amplification in QMA, with the key step written by GPT-5](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-09-25-qma-amplification-limits): A quantum complexity paper proving black-box error amplification for QMA cannot push completeness closer to certainty than doubly exponentially, in which the pivotal technical step of the first version was produced by GPT-5 in about half an hour; the published version replaces that step with a simpler one suggested by a human coauthor. (UT Austin / CWI Amsterdam / University of Bonn, GPT-5 Thinking, 2025-09-25; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [4×4 complex matrix multiplication in 48 scalar multiplications](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-05-alphaevolve-matmul): AlphaEvolve found a scheme multiplying 4×4 complex matrices with 48 scalar multiplications, improving on Strassen's 49 from 1969. (Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve (Gemini-based), 2025-05-14; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [A fully machine-generated paper passed workshop peer review](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-03-12-ai-scientist-workshop-paper): One of three end-to-end AI-generated manuscripts submitted to an ICLR 2025 workshop averaged 6.33 from reviewers and would have been accepted; the authors withdrew it, and the bar cleared was a workshop track, not the main conference. (Sakana AI, The AI Scientist-v2, 2025-03-12; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Improved heuristics for online bin packing](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-12-funsearch-binpacking): FunSearch produced bin-packing heuristics outperforming standard baselines on benchmark distributions. (Google DeepMind, FunSearch (PaLM 2 / Codey), 2023-12-14; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Faster sorting routines discovered and merged into the LLVM C++ library](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-06-07-alphadev): AlphaDev found shorter branchless routines for sorting small fixed-length inputs; reverse-engineered to C++, they were merged into LLVM's libc++, the first change to those routines in over a decade. (Google DeepMind, AlphaDev (AlphaZero-based), 2023-06-07; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Faster matrix-multiplication algorithms found by reinforcement learning](https://whataifound.org/finding/2022-10-05-alphatensor): AlphaTensor discovered matrix-multiplication schemes using fewer scalar multiplications than any previously known, including a way to multiply 4×4 matrices over GF(2) in 47 multiplications versus the 49 of two-level Strassen. (Google DeepMind, AlphaTensor (AlphaZero-based), 2022-10-05; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)

### Materials science

All 4 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/materials

- [Two kagome superconductors predicted by machine learning and confirmed in the lab](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-06-17-kagome-superconductors): A screening pipeline that narrowed over 1.3 million candidate structures picked out YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, which were then synthesized and measured to superconduct at 0.81 K and 0.95 K. (Aalto University / Rice University, Unknown, 2026-06-17; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Generative model designs crystals to order; its flagship synthesis turned out to be a known compound](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-01-16-mattergen): MatterGen generates crystal structures conditioned on target properties, and its headline experimental validation was later shown to match a compound reported in 1972 that sits in the model's own training data. (Microsoft Research, MatterGen, 2025-01-16; verification: Disputed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Large-scale prediction of new stable crystalline materials (GNoME)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-11-29-gnome): GNoME predicted about 2.2 million new inorganic crystal structures, roughly 380,000 of them flagged as thermodynamically stable, presented as an order-of-magnitude expansion of known stable materials. (Google DeepMind, GNoME (graph neural network), 2023-11-29; verification: Disputed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Autonomous laboratory reports solid-state synthesis of new inorganic compounds](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-11-29-a-lab-synthesis): Berkeley's A-Lab, an AI-driven autonomous laboratory, reported synthesising 41 novel inorganic compounds out of 58 targets over 17 days with minimal human intervention. (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, A-Lab (ML planning + robotics), 2023-11-29; verification: Disputed; autonomy: AI-led)

### Mathematics

All 115 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/mathematics

- [Erdős Problem 173: a two-coloring of the plane misses at most one triangle, which is equilateral](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-19-erdos-173-monochromatic-triangles): A Lean-checked proof that in every two-coloring of the plane, every triangle except possibly one equilateral triangle has a monochromatic congruent copy, settling a 1973 conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Montgomery, Rothschild, Spencer and Straus, found by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 working in alternation. (Plasma AI, GPT-6 Astra (Codex) and Claude Opus 5.5 (Claude Code), alternating; Claude Opus 5.5 (Lean formalization), 2026-10-19; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led; machine-checked record: Palomar PALOMAR-2026-10-19-000008)
- [Erdős Problem 111: graphs that are not countably colorable need superlinear deletions to become bipartite](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-19-erdos-111-bipartization): A Lean-checked proof that if every finite subgraph on \(m\) vertices of a graph can be made bipartite by deleting at most \(Cm\) edges, the graph is countably colorable, so \(h_G(n)/n \to \infty\) for every graph of chromatic number \(\aleph_1\), answering the second question of Erdős Problem 111; the proof was found by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 in alternation. - [Erdős problem #728 resolved and formalized in Lean](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-01-erdos-728): GPT-5.2 produced a proof of a previously open Erdős problem; Harmonic's Aristotle formalized it in Lean, making it the first Erdős problem regarded as fully resolved by AI with machine-checked proof. (OpenAI / Harmonic, GPT-5.2 Pro + Aristotle, 2026-01-13; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: Autonomous; open-problem record: MathDB 315787)
- [AlphaEvolve across 67 problems: 20 improvements, 8 regressions](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-11-03-alphaevolve-at-scale): A systematic study with Terence Tao of an evolutionary coding agent on 67 open problems in analysis, combinatorics and geometry, reporting where it beat the literature and where it did not. (Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve (Gemini-based), 2025-11-03; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [GPT-5 "solved 10 Erdős problems": it located existing solutions](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-10-19-gpt5-erdos-retrieval): An OpenAI executive announced that GPT-5 had solved 10 previously open Erdős problems and made progress on 11 more; the problems were only 'open' in the sense that one database maintainer was unaware of the already-published solutions the model surfaced. (OpenAI, GPT-5, 2025-10-19; verification: Already known; autonomy: Retrieval)
- [New families of unstable singularities in fluid equations](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-09-17-unstable-singularities): Physics-informed neural networks found previously unknown unstable self-similar blow-up solutions for three fluid equations, computed to near machine precision, and revealed an unexpected near-linear relation between a solution's instability order and its blow-up rate. (Google DeepMind (with Brown, NYU and Stanford), Physics-informed neural networks with Gauss–Newton optimisation, 2025-09-17; verification: Author verified; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Strong prime number theorem formalized in Lean by an autoformalization agent](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-09-11-gauss-strong-pnt): An agent completed a Lean formalization of the strong prime number theorem in about three weeks, finishing a project two expert mathematicians had left blocked after 18 months. (Math, Inc., Gauss (autoformalization agent), 2025-09-11; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Improved step-size bound in smooth convex optimization](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-08-gpt5-convex-bound): GPT-5 Pro extended a guaranteed-convexity window for gradient descent from \(\eta \le 1/L\) to \(\eta \le 1.5/L\), but the optimal \(1.75/L\) bound had already been published months earlier. (OpenAI, GPT-5 Pro, 2025-08-01; verification: Already known; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Machine-checked Lean proofs for five of six 2025 IMO problems](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-07-28-aristotle-imo-lean): Harmonic's Aristotle produced formally verified Lean 4 proofs for five of the six 2025 IMO problems, so the gold-medal-standard score rests on a compiler rather than on human graders. (Harmonic, Aristotle, 2025-07-28; verification: Formally verified; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Gold-medal standard at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-07-21-gemini-deepthink-imo): An advanced version of Gemini Deep Think read the official problem statements and wrote natural-language proofs for five of the six 2025 IMO problems inside the contest time limits, scoring 35 of 42, graded and certified by the official IMO coordinators. (Google DeepMind, Gemini Deep Think (advanced version), 2025-07-21; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Improved lower bound for the 11-dimensional kissing number](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-05-alphaevolve-kissing): AlphaEvolve improved the best known configuration for the kissing number problem in 11 dimensions. (Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve (Gemini-based), 2025-05-14; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold; open-problem record: MathDB 315951)
- [Improved bound for the Erdős minimum-overlap problem](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-05-alphaevolve-minimum-overlap): AlphaEvolve nudged the best known bound for Erdős's minimum-overlap constant, the first improvement since 2016, and sharpened several autocorrelation inequalities. (Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve (Gemini-based), 2025-05-14; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold; open-problem record: MathDB 316064)
- [Silver-medal standard at the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-07-25-alphaproof-imo): AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 together solved four of the six 2024 IMO problems for 28 of 42 points (one short of the gold threshold), with the algebra and number-theory solutions produced and checked in the Lean proof assistant. (Google DeepMind, AlphaProof + AlphaGeometry 2, 2024-07-25; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Olympiad geometry solved without human demonstrations](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-01-17-alphageometry): A language model trained purely on synthetic data, paired with a symbolic deduction engine, solved 25 of 30 olympiad geometry problems against 10 for the previous best automated system and 25.9 for the average human gold medallist. (Google DeepMind, AlphaGeometry, 2024-01-17; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [New lower bound constructions for the cap set problem](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-12-funsearch-capset): FunSearch discovered larger cap sets than any previously known construction, the first time an LLM-based system produced a genuinely new discovery on an established open problem. (Google DeepMind, FunSearch (PaLM 2 / Codey), 2023-12-14; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Two theorems found by machine pattern-spotting in knot theory and representation theory](https://whataifound.org/finding/2021-12-01-knot-theory-intuition): Networks trained to predict one mathematical invariant from another, then probed for which inputs mattered, pointed mathematicians to a proved theorem linking a knot's signature to a new geometric quantity, and to structure behind the combinatorial invariance conjecture. (Google DeepMind (with Oxford and Sydney), Supervised networks with gradient-based attribution, 2021-12-01; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Reinforcement learning refutes several conjectures in extremal combinatorics](https://whataifound.org/finding/2021-04-29-wagner-combinatorics): A neural network building graphs edge by edge under a cross-entropy search produced explicit counterexamples to several published conjectures in graph theory and extremal combinatorics. (Tel Aviv University, Deep cross-entropy method (custom network), 2021-04-29; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: Search scaffold)

### Medicine

All 22 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/medicine

- [Randomised trial of AI wearable monitoring after heart-failure discharge finds no fall in rehospitalisation (LINK-HF2)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-09-link-hf2-wearable-monitoring-rct): In a randomised trial of 171 veterans discharged after a heart-failure admission at five VA medical centres, alerts from a personalised AI model reading a wearable patch, routed to clinicians with a response algorithm, were feasible but did not reduce heart-failure rehospitalisation (16.3% against 18.7%, hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.43 to 1.84) or a composite of rehospitalisation, emergency visits and death. (US Department of Veterans Affairs / University of Utah, Personalised similarity-based anomaly model on wearable multisensor data, not named in the abstract, 2026-10-09; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04502563)
- [Pragmatic randomised trial of AI-triggered decision support for postoperative delirium finds no effect](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-09-ai-cds-postoperative-delirium-rct): In a pragmatic trial embedded in routine care at Mount Sinai, 7,294 surgical patients flagged as cognitively impaired by a natural-language-processing model, test scores or diagnosis codes were randomised to a non-interruptive decision-support nudge for anaesthesia teams or usual care, with no difference in postoperative delirium (35.1% against 32.7%, P = 0.37) or in adherence to 12 best practices, though fewer than one in five patients were ever assessed for delirium. (Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, Natural-language-processing model for cognitive impairment in health records, not named in the abstract, 2026-10-09; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05777187)
- [AMIE with real patients before urgent primary care visits: a prospective feasibility study](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-08-amie-primary-care-feasibility): In a single-arm study at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, 98 patients completed a text conversation with Google's AMIE in the five days before an urgent primary care visit, under live physician supervision; no conversation needed a safety stop under prespecified criteria, supervisors noted one hallucination, and physicians found the transcript helpful for preparation in 33 of the 44 cases where they reviewed it. (Google / Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), 2026-10-08; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06911398)
- [Physicians steered by a covertly adversarial chatbot made harmful decisions at 49% of targeted points, against 2% with an aligned one](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-07-conversational-ai-subverts-clinical-judgment): In a participant-blinded randomised experiment, 225 neurocritical-care physicians from 42 countries worked through anonymised real cases with a chatbot covertly instructed to steer them either toward predefined harmful options or toward correct ones; the adversarial version raised harmful decisions from 2% to 49% of targeted decision points and cut correct ones from 83% to 25%, and only two physicians reported suspecting manipulation. (University of California, San Francisco / Université Libre de Bruxelles, DeepSeek V4 Flash, 2026-10-07; verification: Claimed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Cluster-randomised trial of an LLM decision-support tool in Kenyan primary care finds no reduction in treatment failure](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-06-26-penda-ai-consult-cluster-rct): In a pragmatic trial at 16 Penda Health clinics in Kenya, clinical officers randomised to a GPT-4o-based decision-support tool in the medical record saw 14-day treatment failure in 2.2% of 4,693 patients against 2.0% of 4,654 without it, an adjusted odds ratio of 0.77 (95% CI 0.55 to 1.08); the tool was safe but did not significantly reduce treatment failure. (KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme / Penda Health / PATH, AI Consult (GPT-4o), 2026-06-26; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Phase 1 trial of a computationally designed pan-sarbecovirus vaccine](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-05-18-pevac-ps-sarbecovirus): A vaccine whose antigen was designed entirely in silico from sarbecovirus sequence data was safe in 39 healthy volunteers and raised immune responses against SARS-CoV-2, SARS, and bat viruses that have never infected humans. (University of Cambridge / DIOSynVax, Unknown, 2026-05-18; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [An antibiotic designed by reinforcement learning clears an MRSA infection in mice](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-04-23-synthecin): A reinforcement-learning generator searching a 46-billion-compound synthesizable space produced synthecin, a structurally novel antibacterial that cleared a methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus wound infection in a mouse model. (McMaster University / Stanford University, SyntheMol-RL, 2026-04-23; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Multicenter prospective validation of Epic's retrained sepsis model (version 2)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-02-02-epic-sepsis-model-v2): Epic's retrained sepsis model, gradient-boosted trees fine-tuned on each hospital's own data, discriminated sepsis at encounter-level AUROCs of 0.82 to 0.92 across 227,091 inpatient encounters at four large US health systems, in line with or above the 0.83 to 0.86 Epic reports internally, but with positive predictive values of only 0.13 to 0.26 and a high alert burden. (Epic Systems, Epic Sepsis Model v2 (gradient-boosted trees with local fine-tuning), 2026-02-02; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Randomised trial of AI-supported mammography screening in 105,934 women (MASAI)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-01-30-masai-ai-mammography): In a Swedish screening trial that randomised 105,934 women, AI triage and detection support found 29% more cancers than standard double reading, cut radiologists' reading workload by 44%, and met its primary endpoint of a non-inferior interval cancer rate, 1.55 against 1.76 per 1,000, with sensitivity of 80.5% against 73.8% at the same 98.5% specificity. (Lund University, Transpara 1.7.0 (ScreenPoint Medical), 2026-01-30; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04838756; regulatory record: FDA AI-enabled devices K210404)
- [Randomised trial of two ambient AI scribes in outpatient practice](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-11-26-ambient-ai-scribes-rct): In a pragmatic three-arm trial of 238 UCLA outpatient physicians, the Nabla scribe cut time spent writing notes by 9.5% against usual care while Microsoft's DAX Copilot made no significant difference; both were associated with modest improvements in burnout and task-load scores, and physicians reported occasional clinically significant inaccuracies with either. (UCLA Health, Microsoft Dragon Ambient eXperience (DAX) Copilot; Nabla, 2025-11-26; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06792890)
- [A generative transformer modelling the course of more than 1,000 diseases (Delphi-2M)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-09-17-delphi-2m-disease-trajectories): A GPT-style model trained on 0.4 million UK Biobank participants predicts each person's rates of more than 1,000 diseases from their past diagnoses, with an average age-stratified AUC of about 0.76 and accuracy comparable to single-disease models, and held up on 1.9 million Danish registry records with no retraining (AUC 0.67 against 0.69 on UK longitudinal testing). (German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) / EMBL-EBI / University of Copenhagen, Delphi-2M (modified GPT-2 architecture), 2025-09-17; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Generative medical event models trained on 118 million patients in Epic Cosmos (CoMET, renamed Curiosity)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-08-16-epic-cosmos-medical-event-models): Decoder-only transformers of up to 1 billion parameters, pretrained on 115 billion medical events from 118 million patients in Epic's Cosmos dataset, followed power-law scaling and, by simulating each patient's next events, generally matched or outperformed task-specific supervised models on 78 clinical prediction tasks without task-specific training. (Epic Systems / Microsoft Research / Yale School of Medicine, Curiosity, first presented as CoMET (Cosmos Medical Event Transformer), up to 1B parameters, 2025-08-16; verification: Claimed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Phase 2a results for a drug whose target and molecule both came from AI](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-06-03-rentosertib-phase2a): Rentosertib, a TNIK inhibitor whose target was picked by one AI system and whose molecule was generated by another, improved forced vital capacity by 98.4 mL at the top dose against a 20.3 mL decline on placebo in a 71-patient randomised trial. (Insilico Medicine, PandaOmics (target) + Chemistry42 (molecule), 2025-06-03; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Randomised comparison of an LLM diagnostic-dialogue system with primary care physicians (AMIE)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2025-04-09-amie-diagnostic-dialogue): In a randomised, double-blind crossover study of text consultations with trained patient-actors across 159 case scenarios, Google's AMIE was more accurate in diagnosis than 20 primary care physicians and was rated better on 30 of 32 axes by specialist physicians and on 25 of 26 axes by the patient-actors. (Google, AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Explorer), fine-tuned from PaLM 2, 2025-04-09; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Autonomous)
- [Zero-shot drug repurposing predictions across 17,080 diseases (TxGNN)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-09-25-txgnn-drug-repurposing): A graph foundation model trained on a medical knowledge graph ranks drugs as likely indications and contraindications for 17,080 diseases, including ones with no approved treatment, improving indication prediction by 49.2% over eight earlier methods under zero-shot evaluation; many of its new predictions match off-label prescribing in 1.27 million patient records at Mount Sinai. (Harvard Medical School, TxGNN (graph neural network with metric learning), 2024-09-25; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Pathogenicity predictions for 71 million human missense variants](https://whataifound.org/finding/2023-09-19-alphamissense): An AlphaFold-derived model classified 89% of all 71 million possible human missense variants as likely benign or likely pathogenic, against the roughly 0.1% that carry a clinical classification today. (Google DeepMind, AlphaMissense, 2023-09-19; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Prospective multi-site study of the TREWS sepsis early-warning system](https://whataifound.org/finding/2022-07-21-trews-sepsis-early-warning): Across five hospitals that monitored 590,736 patients with a machine-learning sepsis alert, patients with sepsis whose alert a clinician confirmed within three hours had 3.3 percentage points lower adjusted in-hospital mortality, an 18.7% relative reduction, than patients whose alert was not confirmed in that time. (Johns Hopkins University, TREWS (Targeted Real-time Early Warning System), 2022-07-21; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; regulatory record: FDA AI-enabled devices K250680)
- [Epic Sepsis Model, version 1, disputed by external validation](https://whataifound.org/finding/2021-06-21-epic-sepsis-model-v1): Epic's proprietary sepsis prediction model, deployed at hundreds of US hospitals with a publicly reported area under the curve of 0.76 to 0.83, scored 0.63 in its first external validation, at Michigan Medicine, missing 67% of sepsis cases while alerting on 18% of all hospitalised patients. (Epic Systems, Epic Sepsis Model v1 (proprietary penalized logistic regression), 2021-06-21; verification: Disputed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Pragmatic randomised trial of an AI-ECG for low ejection fraction in primary care (EAGLE)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2021-05-06-eagle-ai-ecg-low-ejection-fraction): Giving primary care teams the output of an AI that reads routine 12-lead ECGs for signs of a weak heart raised new diagnoses of low ejection fraction within 90 days from 1.6% to 2.1% of 22,641 patients, in a cluster-randomised trial across 120 teams at 45 Mayo Clinic clinics and hospitals, without increasing echocardiogram use overall. (Mayo Clinic, AI-ECG convolutional neural network for left ventricular systolic dysfunction, 2021-05-06; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04000087; regulatory record: FDA AI-enabled devices K232699)
- [Halicin, an antibiotic found by a neural network screening a compound library](https://whataifound.org/finding/2020-02-20-halicin): A graph neural network trained on 2,335 molecules picked halicin out of a repurposing library; it killed multidrug-resistant bacteria including Acinetobacter baumannii and Mycobacterium tuberculosis in vitro and cleared infections in mice. (MIT / Broad Institute, Directed message-passing graph neural network (Chemprop), 2020-02-20; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Baricitinib for COVID-19, named by a knowledge-graph search and confirmed in randomised trials](https://whataifound.org/finding/2020-02-04-baricitinib-covid19): A search of BenevolentAI's machine-learning-built biomedical knowledge graph named the rheumatoid arthritis drug baricitinib as a candidate COVID-19 treatment within weeks of the outbreak; randomised trials run by groups unconnected to BenevolentAI later found it lowered 28-day mortality in hospitalised patients, from 14% to 12% among 8,156 patients in RECOVERY. (BenevolentAI, BenevolentAI biomedical knowledge graph with machine-learning literature extraction, 2020-02-04; verification: Independently checked; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Pivotal trial of an autonomous AI diagnostic for diabetic retinopathy (IDx-DR)](https://whataifound.org/finding/2018-08-28-idx-dr-autonomous-diagnostic): In a prospective trial at 10 US primary care offices, an AI system that grades retinal photographs with no clinician reading them detected more-than-mild diabetic retinopathy with 87.2% sensitivity and 90.7% specificity against a specialist reading-centre reference, exceeding every prespecified endpoint; the results were the basis for the first FDA authorization of an autonomous AI diagnostic. (IDx / University of Iowa, IDx-DR, 2018-08-28; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Autonomous; trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02963441; regulatory record: FDA AI-enabled devices DEN180001)

### Neuroscience

All 1 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/neuroscience

- [Complete wiring diagram of an adult fruit-fly brain](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-10-02-flywire-connectome): Machine segmentation of an electron-microscopy volume, corrected by a large community of proofreaders, produced the first synapse-level map of an entire adult brain: 139,255 neurons and roughly 50 million synapses. (FlyWire Consortium (Princeton, MRC LMB, Cambridge, Vermont), Automated electron-microscopy segmentation networks, 2024-10-02; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-assisted)

### Physics

All 8 in one page: https://whataifound.org/topic/physics

- [36 manuscripts across 18 fields from the BootLoops harness run with Claude](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-10-01-bootloops-manuscripts): Matthew Schwartz's open-source BootLoops harness, operated by Claude, produced 36 manuscripts with 19 coauthors between July and September 2026, mostly exact or certified computations carried from physics and computer science into fields such as population genetics, phylogenetics, ecology and health policy; eight are still in preparation and none is yet listed as published in a journal. (Independent, Claude (the essay names Claude Fable 5 for the initial porting; versions per result are not recorded), 2026-10-01; verification: Claimed; autonomy: AI-assisted)
- [Six-particle MHV amplitude in planar N=4 super Yang-Mills computed at nine loops](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-09-25-nine-loop-hexagon-amplitude): Claude computed the six-particle maximally-helicity-violating amplitude in planar \(\mathcal{N} = 4\) super Yang-Mills theory at nine loops, one loop beyond the previous record, from a single prompt naming the problem. (Anthropic, Claude Fable 5.1 (in Claude Science), 2026-09-25; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Supporting affine functionals for entanglement of formation need not exist](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-27-entanglement-supporting-functional): An explicit two-qubit state has no global supporting affine functional for the entanglement of formation, contradicting an assumption used in several papers. (Independent, Claude Fable 5, 2026-08-27; verification: Author verified; autonomy: AI-assisted; also listed at: vibemathed supporting-affine-functionals-for-entanglement-of-formation)
- [Counterexamples to the fractional colouring conjecture for Pauli shadow tomography](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-08-20-pauli-fractional-colouring): The fractional chromatic number of the anticommutation graph of large-expectation Pauli observables is not bounded by a constant over \(\varepsilon^2\), removing a proposed route to triply efficient shadow tomography. (Independent, GPT-5.6 Sol, 2026-08-20; verification: Author verified; autonomy: Collaborative; also listed at: vibemathed fractional-colouring-pauli-shadow-tomography)
- [Identity for the critical exponents of jamming derived analytically](https://whataifound.org/finding/2026-06-02-jamming-exponent-identity): The relation \(a + b = 1\) between critical exponents at the jamming transition, previously seen only numerically in the full replica-symmetry-breaking solution of hard spheres, is derived from the scaling equations and published after peer review. (Independent, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.7, 2026-06-02; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Collaborative; also listed at: vibemathed fullrsb-jamming-identity)
- [A neural decoder that identifies quantum errors more accurately than hand-designed methods](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-11-20-alphaqubit): A transformer trained on Google's Sycamore surface-code data cut decoding errors by 6% against tensor-network decoding and 30% against correlated matching, the best reported accuracy at the time. (Google DeepMind / Google Quantum AI, AlphaQubit, 2024-11-20; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: AI-led)
- [Reinforcement learning steers a tokamak away from tearing instabilities](https://whataifound.org/finding/2024-02-21-tearing-mode-avoidance): A controller trained on past DIII-D shots forecast tearing-mode instabilities up to 300 ms ahead and adjusted the plasma in real time to avoid them, holding high-performance conditions that would otherwise have collapsed. (Princeton University / PPPL / DIII-D National Fusion Facility, Deep reinforcement learning controller over a learned plasma model, 2024-02-21; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
- [Deep reinforcement learning controls tokamak fusion plasma](https://whataifound.org/finding/2022-02-16-tokamak-plasma-control): A reinforcement-learning controller learned to shape and stabilise the magnetic confinement of real fusion plasma inside the TCV tokamak, holding configurations that are hard to sustain by hand. (Google DeepMind, DeepMind RL controller, 2022-02-16; verification: Peer reviewed; autonomy: Search scaffold)
